chunks: Certainly, the innovations are apparent, having their signs.
And certainly, the worst of people before Allah is an oppressive Imam who has gone astray and through whom others go astray, so he kills an accepted Sunnah and revives an abandoned innovation.

And I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'On the Day of Resurrection, the oppressive Imam will be brought without any supporter or one to advance excuses on his behalf, so he will be thrown into the Fire of Hell, and he will rotate in it as the millstone rotates, then he will be tied in its bottom.'
ai.seo_question: What is the fate of an oppressive Imam who deviates from the Sunnah according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha describes the fate of an oppressive Imam (Imam al-Ja'ir) who deviates from the truth and leads others astray. It highlights his destruction of established Sunnah and revival of Bid'ah, culminating in his eternal punishment in Hell where he will be confined and rotating like a millstone. In Shia exegesis, this 'Imam' often refers specifically to Caliph Uthman ibn Affan, whose governance is critiqued for introducing innovations and neglecting the Prophet's practices, serving as a paradigm for political deviation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Certainly, the worst man before Allāh is the oppressive Imām who has gone astray and through whom others go astray. He destroys the accepted sunnah and revives abandoned innovations.

I heard the Messenger of Allāh saying: “On the Day of Judgement the oppressive Imām will be brought without anyone to support him or anyone to advance excuses on his behalf, and then he will be thrown into Hell where he will rotate as the hand-mill rotates, then (eventually) he will be confined to its hollow.”
